Q: How can I properly handle wildcard expansion in a Bash shell script? A:

There's no need to spawn a shell to look at the $? variable, you can evaluate it directly.

It should just be:

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then

Q: DB2/LUW v11.5.9 Collation names for COLLATION_KEY() function? A:

Look at the Unicode Collation Algorithm based collations article.
It's probably some minor DB2 documentation bug, because this link is provided for the COLLATION_KEY_BIT function description, but not for the COLLATION_KEY one you use.

Update:

But if your goal is to achieve EBCDIC sort order on DB2 for LUW systems (and not how the question is written), then you can't do it with the DB2 COLLATION_KEY[_BIT] functions.
You may create your own function for that:

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION EBCDIC_COLLATION(pstr VARCHAR(255))
RETURNS VARCHAR(255)
DETERMINISTIC
NO EXTERNAL ACTION
CONTAINS SQL
RETURN TRANSLATE(
  pstr
-- EBCDIC sort order is aA0
-- So, reorder should be:
-- Digits to the end    of ASCII: 0123456789 -> qrstuvwxyz 
-- lcase  to the top    of ASCII: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP
-- ucase  to the middle of ASCII: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ -> QRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnop 
, 'qrstuvwxyzQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnop0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP'
-- ASCII sort order is 0Aa:
, '0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
)
;

SELECT 
    str
  , rownumber() OVER (ORDER BY str) AS ascii_order
FROM (VALUES '0', 'a', 'A') t(str)
ORDER BY EBCDIC_COLLATION(str)
;

The result is:

STR ASCII_ORDER
a 3
A 2
0 1

Here is the db<>fiddle link to check the sort order with this approach.

Q: How to set the number of y-axis values displayed when faceting A:

To get more control over the breaks you can write your own breaks function. The following code gives you exactly 3 breaks. However, this very basic approach does not necessarily result in "pretty" breaks: 

library(ggplot2)

my_breaks <- function(x) { 
  seq(0, round(max(x), 0), length.out = 3) 
} 

my_limits <- function(x) { 
  c(x[1], ceiling(x[2]))
}

# Dataset 2
dat <- data.frame(
  ID = c("A", "A", "A","B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C"), 
  A = c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3", "Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3","Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 
  B = c(1.7388, 4.2059, .7751, .9489, 2.23405, .666589, 0.024459, 1.76190, 0.066678)) 

ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = A, y = B)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~ID, scales= "free_y") + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = my_breaks, limits = my_limits)


# Dataset 1
dat <- data.frame(ID = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"),
                  A = c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 1", "Type 2"),
                  B = c(1, 2, 53, 87, 200, 250))

ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = A, y = B)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~ID, scales= "free_y") + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = my_breaks, limits = my_limits)

Q: Dynamic Array to stack blocks of calculations A:

You have some nice answers already, one more exotic than the other.

Maybe this version is pretty straightforward, not using any lambdas:

=LET(data,Table1,L,INDEX(data,,2),T,INDEX(data,,3),W,INDEX(data,,4),H,INDEX(data,,5),VSTACK(TOROW(EXPAND(TAKE(data,,1),,2,"")),WRAPCOLS(TOCOL(INDEX(TOROW(HSTACK(L,L+W,T,T+H)),{1,1,2,2,1,3,4,4,3,3}+SEQUENCE(ROWS(data),,0,4)),1),5)))

Where data is the data of your table, excluding headers.

L is the indexed column of Left values

T is the indexed Top values

W is the indexed Width values

H is the kindexed Height values

Then i take the first column of the table, containing the titles and expand a blank value aside of it and flatten it torow, resulting in 1st value, 1st blank, 2nd value, 2nd blank, etc..

This will be the headers.

I also stack all the Left, the Left+Width, the Top and Top+Height values and flatten them as a column, starting with the 4 values from the first data row, followed by the next 4, etc.

I index these flattened values taking the 1st, 1st, 2nd, 2nd, 1st and 3rd, 4th, 4th, 3rd, 3rd followed by the same index + 4 (so the same index but for values 4 rows lower than the previous, being the next data-row values).

These indexed values are flattened once more, to be able to make use of WRAPCOLS, spilling to the right after every 5th value, so the indexed values per data row are split into 2 separate columns per data-row.

Thanks for this nice challenge.

Q: My Shinydashboard App is not deploying : Bundle does not contain manifest file A:

remove setwd("C:/Users/Baillargeon/Desktop/R_PROG/RShiny_test") as first line. When you are deploying on shinyapps.io , it is a linux environment. so C:/ makes no sense.

Moreover, by default your working directory is where your ui.R and server.R are located. So, your data folder path should be relevant to that. Which looks like so from your code.

read documentation 9.4 “Disconnected from server” messages

Q: How to install specific version rlang? A:

Here are two solutions to try.

Option 1: install latest version

  1. remove rlang using remove.packages("rlang")
  2. shutdown and restart R
  3. reinstall rlang using install.packages("rlang")

Option 2: install specific version

  1. go to the CRAN rlang archive

  2. from the list, copy the URL of the specific version you need

  3. start R, and run install.packages("[URL]", repo=NULL, type="source") e.g.:

install.packages("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/rlang/rlang_0.2.2.tar.gz", repo=NULL, type="source")

Q: add command INSIDE batch file to generate text log (launched by double click) A: 
@if (@CodeSection == @Batch) @then


if defined Restart goto Begin

rem TeeMyself.bat: Send output of this Batch file into screenOut.txt file
rem Antonio Perez Ayala

set Restart=True
call "%~F0" 2>&1 | Cscript //nologo //E:JScript "%~F0" 2>screenOut.txt
set Restart=
goto :EOF

:Begin

rem Place your Batch code here; for example:

rem The date: %date%, the time: %time%
dir TeeMyself.*
rem An error message sent to STDERR
verify bad

goto :EOF


@end


// JScript section

while ( ! WScript.Stdin.AtEndOfStream ) {
   // Read the next line from Stdin
   var line = WScript.Stdin.ReadLine();
   // Duplicate the line to Stdout and Stderr
   WScript.Stdout.WriteLine(line);
   WScript.Stderr.WriteLine(line);

Q: hibernate not-null property references a null or transient value: A:

I think that relationship between the entity Company and the entity Order is the cause of your problem. The entity Order haven't Company.

A question, order.getCompany() could be null during your tests? Your mapping of the entity Order is:

@ManyToOne(**optional = false**, fetch = FetchType.LAZY)

I see that the field Company is required in the entity Order.

Regards
